population structure and related kinship are best estimated relative to the reference set of all alleles in the population of origin, and that this can be done by moment estimators based on allele matches between individuals.

the parameters of population structure, inbreeding and relatedness are defined as probabilities of identity by decent in the target set relative to the reference set, and that these probabilities can be estimated from the data by moment estimators.

the parameters of population structure, inbreeding and relatedness are differences of probabilities of allele matching in target and reference sets and that the reference set for these parameters is the population from which the individuals in a study were sampled.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

population structure is a measure of the extent to which individuals are related within a population, and that kinship is a measure of how individuals differ in their relatedness within the population.
we have shown that the standard definitions and estimates of population structure, inbreeding, and relatedness are not appropriate in a wide variety of applications.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the parameters of population genetic interest are relative, and that it is important to specify clearly the reference set of individuals or populations.

population structure and related kinship parameters are best treated as being relative to some set of alleles, which should be the population of origin for individuals in a study, and that the reference and target sets of alleles can overlap.
population geneticists should be explicit about the set of alleles to which the parameters of interest are relative.
